extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, USPTO patent examiners and USPTO staff who prepare or decide petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and delegation rules in the MPEP for preparing, filing, and deciding petitions to the Director and other USPTO officials, including required content, timing, fees, referral procedures, and which types of petitions are decided by which officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate paper per distinct subject (37 CFR 1.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Since different matters may be considered by different branches or sections of the Office, each distinct subject, inquiry or order must be contained in a separate paper to avoid confusion and delay in answering papers dealing with different subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects provided for on a single Office or WIPO form may be contained in a single paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for petition to the Director (37 CFR 1.181(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition may be taken to the Director: (1) From any action or requirement of any examiner in the ex parte prosecution of an application, or in ex parte or inter partes prosecution of a reexamination proceeding which is not subject to appeal to the PTAB or to the court; (2) In cases in which a statute or the rules specify that the matter is to be determined directly by or reviewed by the Director; and (3) To invoke the supervisory authority of the Director in appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of a petition (MPEP / 37 CFR 1.181 guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition should include: 1) A statement of the type of relief requested and the authorizing provision of statute or rules, if applicable; 2) A statement of the relevant facts; 3) An identification of the points that are to be reviewed; and 4) The fee, where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefs or memoranda, if any, in support thereof should accompany or be embodied in the petition; and where facts are to be proven, the proof in the form of affidavits or declarations (and exhibits, if any) must accompany the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting materials must accompany petition (37 CFR 1.181(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefs/memoranda in support should accompany/ be embodied in the petition; proof of facts (affidavits/declarations and exhibits) must accompany the petition where facts are to be proven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration and repeated action often required before petition (37 CFR 1.181(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition is taken from an action or requirement of an examiner it may be required that there have been a proper request for reconsideration (37 CFR 1.111) and a repeated action by the examiner; the examiner may be directed to furnish a written statement setting forth reasons for the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal statement may be provided to petitioner; informal memorandum might not be mailed to petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement / dismissal if fee missing (37 CFR 1.181(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a fee is required for a petition to the Director the appropriate section will indicate; if any required fee does not accompany the petition, the petition will be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 10.20 may be used where an insufficient fee was filed with a petition or a request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing rarely granted (37 CFR 1.181(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral hearing will not be granted except when considered necessary by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing petition does not stay reply periods or other proceedings (37 CFR 1.181(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere filing of a petition will not stay any period for reply that may be running against the application, nor act as a stay of other proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: filing a petition to vacate a final rejection within 2 months does not extend the reply period; if petition is later granted and applicant filed a timely full reply, the case is not abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness — 2-month filing rule (37 CFR 1.181(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition under this part not filed within two months of the mailing date of the action or notice from which relief is requested may be dismissed as untimely, except as otherwise provided. This two-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month period applies to petitions under any section that does not specify a filing time; it is not extendible under 37 CFR 1.136(a) because the time is within the discretion of the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider in accepting untimely petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Deciding official may accept a petition filed more than 2 months after the action if doing so would avoid unnecessary delays; non-exhaustive factors to consider include: (1) Petitioner engaged in significant, constructive efforts with the examiner to resolve the issue; (2) Examiner agreed on the written record to perform an action that would resolve the issue but failed to do so; (3) Extenuating circumstances (health, pandemic, natural disaster, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepted, the reason for accepting the untimely petition should be articulated in the decision; if dismissed as untimely, the decision should explain how the 2-month period was calculated and inform petitioner of ability to renew arguments in a renewed petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may delegate petition determination (37 CFR 1.181(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may delegate to appropriate Patent and Trademark Office officials the determination of petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegations to various Office officials are set forth in this Chapter. Authority not delegated remains with the Director unless delegated on an ad hoc basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions not provided for decided on merits (37 CFR 1.182)
rubrics_metrics.description: All situations not specifically provided for in the regulations will be decided in accordance with the merits of each situation by or under the authority of the Director, subject to other requirements; any petition seeking decision under this section must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension/waiver of rules in extraordinary situations (37 CFR 1.183)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an extraordinary situation, when justice requires, any requirement of the regulations which is not a requirement of the statutes may be suspended or waived by the Director or designee, sua sponte or on petition, subject to other requirements; any petition under this section must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph for Petition Header (Form paragraph 10.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 10.30 may be used to generate header information for a petition decision (In re Application of: [1] : Appl. No.: [2] : DECISION ON PETITION Filed: [3] : [5] For: [4] ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for handling petitions (MPEP § 1002.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions, together with the respective application files, are sent to the official having the delegated authority to decide the petition; the petition may be referred to the examiner for a formal statement under 37 CFR 1.181(c) or for an informal memorandum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a formal statement is made, a copy is mailed to the petitioner by the examiner unless otherwise directed, and the application file and petition, accompanied by the examiner’s statement, are returned to the official handling the petition. If an informal memorandum is requested, no copy is mailed to the petitioner by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegations do not confer right to decision by a specific official
rubrics_metrics.description: The delegations set forth in this Chapter do not confer a right to have a matter decided by a specific Office official; such delegations aid in efficient treatment of petitions by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A delegation of supervisory or higher level review authority over a matter carries with it the authority to decide the matter ab initio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality language for delegated denials and dismissals
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where authority to decide petitions has been delegated (certain MPEP sections), a denial of a petition is a final agency decision; a dismissal or denial without prejudice and other interlocutory orders are not final agency decisions. A petition decided under some delegated authorities (e.g., TC Director) should not use language suggesting it is a final agency decision and should be dismissed rather than denied when relief is not granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested dismissal language for Technology Center Director decisions: 'The petition filed [date X] is dismissed. This is not a final agency decision. See MPEP § 1002.02. Any request for reconsideration or higher level review of this decision not filed within two months of the mailing date of this decision may be dismissed as untimely. This two-month period is not extendable. See 37 CFR 1.181(f).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions decided by Deputy Commissioner (Mail Stop Petition guidance and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, petitions under the Deputy Commissioner who oversees the Office of Petitions should be directed to 'Mail Stop Petition, Commissioner for Patents' except as otherwise provided (e.g., Hatch-Waxman PTE directed to Mail Stop Hatch-Waxman PTE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: revive abandoned application — unintentional delay (37 CFR 1.137)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to revive an abandoned national, nonprovisional or provisional patent application on the basis of unintentional delay, 37 CFR 1.137 and MPEP § 711.03(c), are decided by the Deputy Commissioner who oversees the Office of Petitions or assigned staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: waiver or suspension of rules (37 CFR 1.183)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.183 for waiver or suspension of rules not otherwise provided for are decided by the Deputy Commissioner who oversees the Office of Petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: invoke supervisory authority under 37 CFR 1.181
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to invoke the supervisory authority of the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 in matters not otherwise provided for are decided by the Deputy Commissioner who oversees the Office of Petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: unintentionally delayed foreign priority claim (37 CFR 1.55(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for an unintentionally delayed foreign priority claim, 37 CFR 1.55(e) and MPEP § 214.02, are handled by the Deputy Commissioner or assigned staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: restore right of foreign priority (37 CFR 1.55(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to restore the right of foreign priority, 37 CFR 1.55(c) and MPEP § 213.03, subsection III, are decided by the Deputy Commissioner or assigned staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: late filing of certified copy of foreign application (37 CFR 1.55(f)/(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for late filing of certified copy of foreign application, 37 CFR 1.55(f) or (g), as applicable, and MPEP § 215.02, are in the Deputy Commissioner's jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: unintentionally delayed domestic benefit claim (37 CFR 1.78(c), (e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for an unintentionally delayed domestic benefit claim, 37 CFR 1.78(c) and (e) and MPEP § 211.04, are decided by the Deputy Commissioner or assigned staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: restore benefit of provisional application (37 CFR 1.78(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to restore the benefit of a provisional application, 37 CFR 1.78(b) and MPEP § 211.01(a), subsection II, are handled by the Deputy Commissioner or assigned staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: defer issuance of patents (37 CFR 1.314)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to defer issuance of patents, 37 CFR 1.314 and MPEP § 1306.01, are decided under the Deputy Commissioner authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: express abandonment after issue fee paid (37 CFR 1.313(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for express abandonment of patent applications after payment of the issue fee, 37 CFR 1.313(c)(3), MPEP § 711.01 subsection and MPEP § 1308, fall under the Deputy Commissioner's jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: restore unintentionally delayed maintenance fee payment in expired patent (37 CFR 1.378)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to accept an unintentionally delayed payment of maintenance fee in an expired patent, 37 CFR 1.378 and MPEP § 2590, are under the Deputy Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: requests for access to patent applications (37 CFR 1.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for access to patent applications under 37 CFR 1.14 (with exceptions for PTAB-related applications) are decided by the Deputy Commissioner (see MPEP §§ 103, 104, 1901.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: expunge papers or assignment information (37 CFR 1.59 / 1.182)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to expunge papers or assignment information from patent applications under 37 CFR 1.59 which were not submitted under specified MPEP sections, and petitions to expunge recorded assignment information under 37 CFR 1.182, are handled by the Deputy Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: Make Special (inventor health or age) and prioritized examination (37 CFR 1.102 / MPEP § 708.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to Make Special based on inventor's health or age, and requests for prioritized examination under 37 CFR 1.102 and MPEP § 708.02, are decided by the Deputy Commissioner or assigned staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: participation requests (PPH, Law School Pilot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for participation in a Patent Prosecution Highway program (PPH) and requests for participation in the Law School Pilot Program are handled under this delegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: Hatch-Waxman patent term extension and related petitions (35 U.S.C. 156; 37 CFR 1.710-1.791)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications relating to Hatch-Waxman patent term extension and petitions relating thereto (including petitions under 37 CFR 1.182/1.183) fall under the Deputy Commissioner or assigned staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: review of Technology Center Director or Central Reexamination Unit Director decisions (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to review a decision of a Technology Center Director or Central Reexamination Unit Director under 37 CFR 1.181 are decided by the Deputy Commissioner or assigned staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: petitions relating to filing date, conversion of application types (37 CFR 1.53, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions relating to the filing date of patent applications under 37 CFR 1.53, conversion of nonprovisional to provisional (and vice versa) where the case is before the Office of Petitions or OLPA, and related matters are handled by the Deputy Commissioner or assigned staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(b) in applications before the Office of Petitions or the Office of Patent Legal Administration are decided by the Deputy Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: withdraw application from issue (37 CFR 1.313) (pre- and post-issue fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions or requests (including USPTO-initiated ones) to withdraw patent applications from issue under 37 CFR 1.313 before or after payment of the issue fee (with the subsections noted) are handled under this delegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: requests to order Director reexamination proceeding (37 CFR 1.520)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to order a Director reexamination proceeding under 37 CFR 1.520 are within the Deputy Commissioner's or assigned staff's delegated matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition category: petitions concerning patent term adjustment and reinstatement (37 CFR 1.704/1.705)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for reconsideration of patent term adjustment indicated in the notice of allowance or in the patent (37 CFR 1.705) and requests for reinstatement of the period of patent term adjustment reduced pursuant to 37 CFR 1.704(b) under 37 CFR 1.705(c) are decided under this delegation (see MPEP § 2734).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters submitted to Technology Center Directors (MPEP § 1003 list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain matters must be submitted to the appropriate Technology Center Director, including requests for certificate of correction raising a novel issue or for patents known to be in litigation; return of papers entered in the file wrapper; certain double patenting rejections on divisionals; requests for patentability reports; actions which hold claims unpatentable affecting corresponding claims in a patent; interferences between applications neither in condition for allowance; and others listed in MPEP § 1003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1003 for the complete list and cross-references to full treatment sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions requiring primary examiner attention (MPEP § 1004 list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing practice requires the primary examiner to be personally responsible for actions including: allowances; examiner’s amendments; Quayle actions; final rejections; withdrawal of final rejection; actions on amendments submitted after final rejection; examiner’s answers on appeal; actions reopening prosecution; requests for withdrawal from issue; 37 CFR 1.312 amendments directed to formal matters or cancellation of claims; rejection of previously allowed claim; holding of abandonment for insufficient reply; classification of allowed cases; treatment of newly filed application that obviously fails to comply with 35 U.S.C. 112; consideration of patentability report; decision on affidavits or declarations; first request for suspension of examiner’s action; decision on reissue oath or declaration; International Preliminary Examination Reports; and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For matters decided by supervisory patent examiners, see MPEP § 1002.02(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to partial signatory authority (MPEP § 1005 list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners with partial signatory authority are expected to sign their own actions except for specified actions which require signature of a primary examiner, Technology Center Director, or practice specialist, including allowances; examiner’s amendments; Quayle actions; final rejections; examiner’s amendments; decisions involving affidavit/declaration evidence; suspension of examiner’s action; reissue applications and actions; requests for extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(b); reexamination proceedings; International Preliminary Examination Reports; actions suggesting claims for interference; and actions involving copied patent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on dismissing vs denying petitions under delegated authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition decided under delegated authority set forth in certain MPEP sections should not use language that suggests a final agency decision; a petition decided by a Technology Center Director in which the requested relief is not granted should be dismissed rather than denied and the decision should indicate that it is not a final agency decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested language is provided to promote consistency and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to refer petitions to the examiner for statement (MPEP § 1002.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions may be referred to the examiner for a formal statement under 37 CFR 1.181(c) or for an informal memorandum; if a formal statement is made, a copy is mailed to the petitioner unless otherwise directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 711.03(d) for more on examiner statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deciding official should articulate reasons for exceptional actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a deciding official accepts an untimely petition or dismisses a petition as untimely, the decision should include an explanation (e.g., reason for acceptance or how the 2-month period was calculated) to ensure clarity of the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should inform petitioner about ability to renew or present arguments in a renewed petition.
